Retrieved 2026-07-20 via Exa search highlights. (Context/background for Hormuz shipping-security angle.)

UK and France leading a multinational reassurance mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz, working with Oman. Britain's main asset: Royal Fleet Auxiliary ship RFA Lyme Bay, converted into a "minehunting mother ship" (270+ personnel: RFA seafarers, 100+ RN mine-warfare/diving/EOD experts, medics, Royal Marines, Army, French sailors) with drones, mine-clearance divers, Merlin helicopters. Air-defence destroyer HMS Dragon escorting; German command ship FGS Mosel and minehunter FGS Fulda also involved. Likely logistics hub: Oman's Port of Duqm. Contributions from Italy, Denmark, Canada.

QUOTE - Foreign Office minister Hamish Falconer (House of Commons, 9 July): "Our priority now is ensuring unimpeded transit passage through the Strait without the threat of violence, tolls, fees or conditions... We want a durable, negotiated peace and the Strait of Hormuz to fully reopen."

Background: Trump proposed a 20% toll on all cargo through Hormuz, calling US "THE GUARDIAN OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT"; UK Lib Dems branded it "state-backed highway robbery." Original US-Iran deal provided only 60 days of toll-free passage. Starmer (then PM) had warned Hormuz disruption could raise UK winter energy bills.
